_comment: Speeds are pixels per simulation tick; multiply by 60 for pixels per second.
A tile is 16 pixels, so the hero's 1.7 is about six and a half tiles a second.
Every enemy is slower than the hero. That is the deal the whole fight rests
on: you can always disengage, so getting hit is a decision you made rather
than something the arena did to you.
aggro is in pixels -- how far an enemy notices you from.

hero.name: Hero
_heal: Health recovered on clearing a stage. Damage carries between stages, so
this is the dial deciding whether that is tense or punishing: at 0 a
single bad stage ends the run three stages later, at 100 stages stop
22 is the tightest value that still clears every seed with a skilled
hero -- measured, not guessed. At 15 the floor breaks (7/8 runs), and at
30 the worst run still finishes on 74hp, which is not a run that was ever
in danger. Rerun tools/balance.py after changing it.

grunt.name: Grunt
grunt._comment: Straightforward pressure. Walks at you, swings when close.

charger.name: Charger
_comment: Slow until it commits, then faster than you. Punishes standing in a line
with it. The long windup on 'gore' is the tell you dodge on.

archer.name: Archer
archer._comment: Punishes standing still in the open. Backs away when you close.

boss.name: The Warden
_comment: Slower than anything else in the game and much harder to kill, so the
fight lasts long enough for its three attacks to become a pattern you
read rather than three things that happen to you.
aggro covers the whole arena -- there is no sneaking up on it, and no
corner it forgets about you in.
Below half health it stops pausing between attacks (see game/ai.py). That
is the whole phase system: no new moves to learn at the moment you are
least able to learn them, just less room to breathe.
